title: Carob: Ancient Carob Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: A Mediterranean tree grown for its pods. Malta calls the Xemxija carob a thousand years old; its measured trunk, 7.25 metres round, says centuries.
intro: The carob is a Mediterranean tree better known for its pods than its bulk, so a trunk four metres round is a big one. Malta calls the Xemxija carob a thousand years old, a figure that may come from a poem on the wall below it; its stems measure 7.25 metres round, which puts it somewhere between four centuries and the legend. Beside a drove road north of Cordoba, a carob the Junta de Andalucia puts at 350 to 400 years has let its limbs down to the ground until the crown closes over its trunks like a vault. In Barcelona's Park Guell, Gaudi ran his viaduct's stone columns around a young carob instead of clearing it, and a second one there is a shoot from around 1907, ringed by the remains of the giant it replaced. Agrigento's Carob of Jupiter stands by the ruined Temple of Olympian Zeus.
